subject: Pharmacology
subtopic: Biologic agents: monoclonal antibodies, small molecule inhibitors, interleukin modulators
vignette: A 67-year-old man with CD20-positive B-cell lymphoma receives rituximab, an agent whose name ends in -ximab, as part of his chemotherapy regimen.
question: What does the -ximab ending and this agent's composition indicate?

options.text: A chimeric human-mouse monoclonal antibody
A humanized monoclonal antibody with only murine complementarity-determining regions
A fully human monoclonal antibody
A small molecule inhibitor targeting intracellular tyrosine kinases
A proteasome inhibitor used in plasma cell dyscrasias

explanation_correct: Drugs ending in -ximab (eg, rituximab) are chimeric human-mouse monoclonal antibodies, meaning their constant regions are human while the variable regions are murine. Rituximab targets the CD20 antigen on B cells and is used in CD20-positive B-cell lymphomas. This nomenclature is a mnemonic for how much of the molecule is of murine origin.

explanation_incorrect.B: Humanized monoclonal antibodies end in -zumab (eg, bevacizumab), with only the antigen-binding loops of murine origin.
explanation_incorrect.C: Fully human monoclonal antibodies end in -umab (eg, denosumab).
explanation_incorrect.D: Small molecule kinase inhibitors end in -tinib (eg, imatinib) and are not antibodies.
explanation_incorrect.E: Proteasome inhibitors end in -zomib (eg, bortezomib), used in multiple myeloma.

educationalObjective: Monoclonal antibody suffixes encode origin: -ximab is chimeric, -zumab humanized, and -umab fully human.

subject: Pharmacology
subtopic: Biologic agents: monoclonal antibodies, small molecule inhibitors, interleukin modulators
vignette: A 44-year-old man presents with a markedly elevated leukocyte count and basophilia. Bone marrow testing reveals the BCR-ABL fusion transcript. He is started on imatinib, an oral agent whose name ends in -tinib.
question: Which of the following best describes this class of agents?

options.text: Monoclonal antibodies that target overexpressed cell surface receptors
Proteasome inhibitors that cause accumulation of misfolded proteins in malignant plasma cells
Small molecule inhibitors of tyrosine kinases that target intracellular signaling molecules
Poly(ADP-ribose) polymerase inhibitors that exploit defects in homologous recombination repair
BRAF kinase inhibitors used in melanoma with activating BRAF mutations

explanation_correct: Drugs ending in -tinib (eg, imatinib) are small molecule tyrosine kinase inhibitors that target intracellular molecules. Imatinib specifically inhibits the constitutively active BCR-ABL tyrosine kinase produced by the Philadelphia chromosome fusion in chronic myeloid leukemia, explaining this patient's presentation.

explanation_incorrect.A: Monoclonal antibodies end in -mab (ximab/zumab/umab) and act on cell surface targets; their large size prevents intracellular access.
explanation_incorrect.B: Proteasome inhibitors end in -zomib (eg, bortezomib) and are used in multiple myeloma.
explanation_incorrect.D: PARP inhibitors end in -parib (eg, olaparib), used in BRCA-mutated tumors.
explanation_incorrect.E: BRAF inhibitors end in -rafenib (eg, vemurafenib); imatinib targets BCR-ABL, not BRAF.

educationalObjective: The suffix -tinib identifies small molecule tyrosine kinase inhibitors such as imatinib against BCR-ABL.

subject: Pharmacology
subtopic: Biologic agents: monoclonal antibodies, small molecule inhibitors, interleukin modulators
vignette: A 71-year-old postmenopausal woman with severe osteoporosis and contraindications to bisphosphonates is prescribed denosumab, a subcutaneous injection whose name ends in -umab.
question: Which of the following best describes this medication?

options.text: A bisphosphonate that binds hydroxyapatite and inhibits osteoclast activity
A fully human monoclonal antibody against RANKL that inhibits osteoclast formation
A selective estrogen receptor modulator that reduces bone resorption
A recombinant human parathyroid hormone analog that stimulates bone formation
A humanized monoclonal antibody against vascular endothelial growth factor

explanation_correct: Drugs ending in -umab are fully human monoclonal antibodies. Denosumab is a fully human monoclonal antibody against RANKL; blocking RANKL prevents osteoclast differentiation and activation, decreasing bone resorption and fracture risk in osteoporosis.

explanation_incorrect.A: Bisphosphonates end in -dronate (eg, alendronate) and act directly on osteoclasts bound to hydroxyapatite; this patient could not take them.
explanation_incorrect.C: SERMs such as raloxifene reduce bone resorption via estrogen receptor agonism in bone and are not monoclonal antibodies.
explanation_incorrect.D: Recombinant PTH analogs such as teriparatide are anabolic agents, not -umab antibodies.
explanation_incorrect.E: Anti-VEGF activity describes bevacizumab, a humanized (-zumab) antibody used in oncology.

educationalObjective: The suffix -umab identifies fully human monoclonal antibodies such as denosumab (anti-RANKL).

subject: Pharmacology
subtopic: Biologic agents: monoclonal antibodies, small molecule inhibitors, interleukin modulators
vignette: A 52-year-old woman with a germline BRCA1 mutation completes platinum-based chemotherapy for ovarian cancer and is placed on maintenance therapy with an oral agent whose name ends in -parib.
question: What is the mechanism of action of this maintenance agent?

options.text: Formation of DNA cross-links between adjacent guanine residues
Stabilization of microtubules, blocking mitotic spindle disassembly
Inhibition of aromatase, lowering peripheral estrogen production
Inhibition of cyclin-dependent kinases, arresting tumor cells in G1 phase
Inhibition of poly(ADP-ribose) polymerase, exploiting defective homologous recombination repair

explanation_correct: Drugs ending in -parib (eg, olaparib) are PARP inhibitors. PARP repairs single-strand DNA breaks; inhibiting it in cells with BRCA-mutated, defective homologous recombination repair creates synthetic lethality, making PARP inhibitors effective maintenance therapy for BRCA-mutated ovarian cancer after platinum response.

explanation_incorrect.A: DNA cross-linking describes platinum compounds ending in -platin (eg, cisplatin), the chemotherapy just completed.
explanation_incorrect.B: Microtubule stabilization describes taxanes ending in -taxel (eg, paclitaxel).
explanation_incorrect.C: Aromatase inhibition describes drugs ending in -trozole (eg, anastrozole), used in estrogen receptor–positive breast cancer.
explanation_incorrect.D: CDK inhibition describes drugs ending in -ciclib (eg, palbociclib), used in hormone receptor–positive breast cancer.

educationalObjective: The suffix -parib identifies PARP inhibitors, which are synthetically lethal in homologous recombination repair–deficient (BRCA-mutated) tumors.

subject: Pharmacology
subtopic: Biologic agents: monoclonal antibodies, small molecule inhibitors, interleukin modulators
vignette: A 58-year-old man with metastatic renal cell carcinoma is treated with aldesleukin, a recombinant agent whose name ends in -leukin. He develops marked capillary leak and hypotension during therapy but shows tumor regression.
question: Which of the following best describes the mechanism of this agent?

options.text: Antagonism of the interleukin-1 receptor, suppressing systemic inflammation
Neutralization of tumor necrosis factor-alpha in the peripheral circulation
Blockade of the interleukin-6 receptor, reducing B-cell activation
Interleukin-2 agonism, stimulating proliferation and activation of T lymphocytes
Inhibition of the proteasome, causing death of malignant plasma cells

explanation_correct: Drugs ending in -leukin (eg, aldesleukin) are interleukin-2 agonists/analogues. Aldesleukin is recombinant IL-2 that activates T lymphocytes and natural killer cells, producing an antitumor immune response in metastatic renal cell carcinoma and melanoma. Its profound immune activation explains the capillary leak syndrome observed here.

explanation_incorrect.A: Interleukin-1 receptor antagonism describes anakinra, which ends in -kinra and is used in autoinflammatory disease, not renal cell carcinoma.
explanation_incorrect.B: TNF-alpha neutralization describes monoclonal antibodies such as infliximab (a chimeric -ximab), used in autoimmune disease.
explanation_incorrect.C: Interleukin-6 receptor blockade describes tocilizumab, an -umab antibody used in rheumatoid arthritis.
explanation_incorrect.E: Proteasome inhibition describes -zomib drugs (eg, bortezomib), used in multiple myeloma.

educationalObjective: The suffix -leukin identifies interleukin-2 agonists (aldesleukin); -kinra identifies interleukin receptor antagonists (anakinra).
